sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Apache Junction
sections.html:
Sellers in Apache Junction can hire an agent, go it alone, or accept a cash offer. The route matters less than three other things: the condition of the house, the state of the title, and whether the buyer needs a lender. A buyer who takes the house as-is and pays without a loan can skip the steps that slow a conventional sale.

The people selling range from retirees downsizing to heirs settling a parent's house, and owners live in most of the homes. Before you speak with a buyer, line up three things.

  • Gather the parcel number, the deed and any HOA or park paperwork.
  • Find out, in writing, which side pays recording and title charges under each offer.
  • Set each offer next to the net a listing would leave after repairs and carrying costs. The list price isn't the number to compare.

By July 1, 2025 the estimate reached 45,672 residents, an 18.6 percent gain on the 38,499 counted in April 2020. A small piece of the city, the El Dorado Mobile Estates Resort and Senior Cottages, reaches into Maricopa County. In October 2021 the city annexed about ten square miles to the south, so some newer addresses sit on recently added land.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit before selling?
sections.html:
Selling needs no permit. Past work on the house is another matter. The city's Division of Building Safety and Inspection takes permit applications through an online system called MyGovernmentOnline, and it posts separate guides for new homes and additions, remodels, pools, manufactured homes and trade work.

The city's residential FAQ offers these rules of thumb:

  • A fence under 6 feet tall needs no permit, though fences in federally patented easements or across drainage ways get a zoning review.
  • A shed of 120 square feet or less with no utilities needs no permit. Larger sheds, garages and workshops do.
  • Patio covers, awnings, carports and room additions need a building permit and must meet setback rules.
  • Flow-restricting walls are not allowed in FEMA special flood hazard areas, so only open, flow-through fencing fits there.

A guest house is allowed on some single-family lots but must be used by family and can't be a separate rental. If you aren't sure a past project was permitted, call Building Safety before a buyer's inspector raises the question. You'll need the parcel number, which the Pinal County Assessor or city planning staff can supply.

sections.h2: Renting the house while you wait to sell
sections.html:
You can. The city's business license form says single family residential rentals need no city application or fee. Other business activity takes a $50 license per activity, renewed each year, and owners with taxable income are pointed to the Arizona Department of Revenue's transaction privilege tax pages. Ask the City Clerk's Office or the Planning and Zoning Division whether stays under 30 days are handled differently at your address.

Tenants affect closing. The city's rental resources page summarizes the federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act, which requires 90 days of notice and lets many bona fide tenants stay through the lease term after a foreclosure sale. Anyone buying a tenant-occupied house with cash should read the lease before settling on a closing date.

sections.h2: Property taxes when the house sells
sections.html:
Most of the city gets its tax bill from the Pinal County Treasurer. Anything over $100 may be paid in two parts. Part one is due October 1 and slips into delinquency after 5 pm on November 1; part two is due March 1 and slips after 5 pm on May 1. Small bills of $100 or less are due in one payment on October 1 and go delinquent after 5 pm on December 31. Paying a full year by December 31 also avoids interest.

A deadline landing on a weekend or holiday shifts to the next business day. After that, 16 percent a year accrues, figured at 1.33 percent for each month or part of one.

If part of your lot or home is in the Maricopa County portion, that treasurer's calendar governs it instead, so check the county printed on your bill. A mortgage holder typically pays the taxes. Exemptions for widows, widowers, disabled owners and some disabled former service members run through the county assessor. If you dispute the valuation, you have 60 days from the Notice of Value.

sections.h2: Recording and transfer steps in Pinal County
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Pinal County Recorder. A transfer of real property travels with an Affidavit of Property Value, except when A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts it. In that case the deed itself carries the statute number and exemption code, as in A.R.S. 11-1134 B3. On the affidavit, enter the day the contract was signed as the sale date. Closing day is the wrong one.

The Recorder's posted fee, effective July 1, 2019, is $30 for documents required or allowed by law to be recorded, and it includes the affidavit fee. Each recording fee also carries $1 for postage to mail documents back. Confirm the amount with the Recorder before mailing a check.

  • Seller: signs the deed and affidavit and hands the title company the parcel number.
  • Buyer or escrow: records the deed and confirms the new mailing address with the Assessor.
  • Both: confirm which share of the year's tax bill each side owes at closing.

A fast sale here still follows a set order. You collect the deed, parcel number and any HOA or park paperwork. You weigh the offers side by side. You pick a buyer and sign a contract, which fixes the sale date used on the affidavit. Escrow pays off the tax balance and any loan, then the deed goes on record with the Pinal County Recorder. Because a cash buyer doesn't wait on a lender, the stretch between contract and closing is usually shorter than with a financed buyer.

If the house has tenants, an open permit or a lot that straddles the county line, say so up front. Each of those changes who you call and what the closing needs, and each is easier to handle before the contract than after it.

faqs.q: Does Apache Junction require a license to rent out a single-family house?
faqs.a: Not for a single family residential rental: the city asks for no application and no fee. Any other business activity costs $50 per activity each year. For stays under 30 days, check with the city.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed before I sell?
faqs.a: A shed of 120 square feet or less with no utilities is fine without one. Bigger buildings, or any with utilities, need a permit, and all sheds must meet setbacks. When in doubt, phone Building Safety.

faqs.q: When are Pinal County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1 starts the first half, which is late after 5 pm on November 1. March 1 starts the second, late after 5 pm on May 1. Bills of $100 or less are paid in full on October 1 and are late after December 31.

faqs.q: What paperwork records the sale of an Apache Junction house?
faqs.a: The Pinal County Recorder receives a deed plus an Affidavit of Property Value, unless an exemption code is written on the deed. Recording costs $30 per document.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether past work on my house was permitted?
faqs.a: Phone the city's Division of Building Safety and Inspection and give your parcel number. Do this early, so any open item can be closed before an inspector finds it.
